architecture.mechanism: Closed-loop PID-controlled variable frequency drive (VFD) airflow regulation that reduces air pulsation and stabilizes air-fuel ratio by maintaining target charge air pressure and temperature.
architecture.intervention: Apply a closed-loop PID controller with a variable frequency drive to the fuel pump's drive/motor or to a bypass line in the fuel flow system, actively regulating fuel pressure and flow rate to maintain target values and damp pulsation during transient demands (e.g., idle, turn maneuvers).
architecture.expected_effect: Stabilized fuel delivery under transient loads eliminates intermittent fuel starvation that causes engine stall during low-speed/low-demand conditions, while precise flow control prevents over-pressurization that could lead to fuel leaks and fire hazard.
architecture.falsification_test: On a chassis dynamometer, install a fuel pressure transducer at the rail and an AFR sensor; run repeated stall-prone transient cycles (idle-to-turn, rapid throttle tip-in/out) with and without the PID/VFD control active. If fuel pressure deviation > ±5 kPa and AFR excursion > ±0.5 persist with the controller enabled, or if stall events still occur at the same rate, the mechanism is falsified.
